descripcion_geo: The 'Great Sea' of the Bible, also called 'Sea of ​​the West'. Western frontier of the promised land and artery of ancient trade.
importancia_estrategica: Western border of Israel and axis of trade between Canaan, Phoenicia, Greece and Rome.

historias.titulo: The sea as the western border of the promised land
historias.descripcion: God points to the Great Sea as the western border of Israel's inheritance: 'from the desert to this sea.'

historias.titulo: Jonah throws into the sea in a storm
historias.descripcion: Jonah, fleeing to Tarshish across the Mediterranean, is thrown into the sea by sailors during a storm; a big fish swallows it.
Paul shipwrecked on the way to Rome in the Mediterranean; The ship runs aground in Malta but everyone is saved.

personajes.descripcion: He tried to flee to Tarshish through the Mediterranean; He was rescued from the bottom of the sea by a large fish.
The Phoenicians dominated Mediterranean trade; Hiram supplied wood to Solomon by sea.
He made three missionary trips through the Mediterranean and was shipwrecked on the way to Rome.

contexto_religioso.contexto_lugar: The sea was for Israel the border of the known world and the scene of Jonah's flight; in the NT, the Pauline mission highway.

judaismo.descripcion: Jonah in the belly of the fish at the bottom of the Mediterranean: symbol of death and resurrection, prayer from the abyss.
judaismo.significado_teologico: Jonah in the belly of the fish at the bottom of the Mediterranean: symbol of death and resurrection, prayer from the abyss.

cristianismo.descripcion: Jesus cites the 'sign of Jonah' as ​​an announcement of his death and resurrection (Mt 12:40).
cristianismo.significado_teologico: Jesus cites the 'sign of Jonah' as ​​an announcement of his death and resurrection (Mt 12:40).

islam.descripcion: Yunus (Jonah) is a prophet in Islam; the Quran tells his story at sea (Cor 37:139-148).
islam.significado_teologico: Yunus (Jonah) is a prophet in Islam; the Quran tells his story at sea (Cor 37:139-148).
